content:
Apple Books is my favorite reading app, and iOS 27.2 brings a few nice design updates. Here's what's new.

Here are the changes iOS 27.2 beta 3 brings to Apple Books

Likely in anticipation of the iPhone Duo being an excellent reading device, Apple has prepared a number of upcoming design updates for its Books app.

iOS 27.2 beta 3 introduces these changes, all related to the reading experience itself.

While reading a book, iOS 27.2 brings the following design updates:

  • You can now track your reading position via a progress bar
  • The menu in the bottom right has been replaced with a new three-dot icon and redesigned as a standard Liquid Glass menu, consistent with other apps
  • Bookmarks have been removed from that menu and moved to the top right as their own button
  • The 'X' button has moved to the top left
  • The 'back' button has moved to the bottom left, and is larger than before

These are only minor updates, but in my experience using them, they are definitely welcome improvements.

I never understood why bookmarks were tucked away in the old menu, so I'm glad to see them made more prominent again. I also really like the new progress bar.

I hope that if iPhone Duo is well received, Apple will see it as an opportunity to invest more in the Books app. Kindle dominates the e-reader market, but I've always preferred Apple's apps and ecosystem, whether for ebooks or audiobooks.

Do you use Apple Books? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.
